text:
anya: Heads up — CI on infra/gitops just failed during the apply step for the gpu-nodepool rollout. GHA shows a concurrency collision and a bunch of `resource already exists` + network timeout errors.
kevin: saw it too, error snippet: `Error: Error waiting for Network Interface: timeout while waiting for state` then terraform retries hit `http 409` on the same nodepool resource.
maria: could be a double-apply race — two runs ended up trying to scale the same dedicated GPU pool. Are we missing a concurrency group on this workflow?
sam: workflow does have `concurrency: group: ${{ github.ref }}` but the gitops manifests trigger multiple PRs and sometimes the apply job gets retried by the self-heal job. logs show two applies ~30s apart.
anya: exact logs: ```Apply started at 2026-03-08T12:05:02Z
module.node_pool.aws_autoscaling_group.gpu: Creating...
Error: RequestLimitExceeded: Rate exceeded
status code: 400, request id: abc-123
...then later...
Error: Error waiting for Autoscaling Group (gpu-pool): timeout while waiting for state
```
kevin: Oof. Rate limiting + partial creates -> when the second apply runs it sees some resources present and hits 409. That explains `resource already exists`.
maria: short-term fix: restrict concurrency to the repo+env+workflow run id so concurrent PR merges won't overlap. Longer-term we need apply idempotency and stronger locking.
sam: we could add a repo-level GHA semaphore using `concurrency: group: infra-apply-${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}` and `cancel-in-progress: false` so retries don't cancel? but that only serializes per-branch.
anya: also noticed the Helm chart upgrade for gpu-driver had `wait: true` and times out if node isn't ready; combined with terraform scaling the node pool it creates a chicken-and-egg. helm fails, gha retriggers, another apply.
kevin: suggestion: split scaling (terraform) + k8s helm rollout into separate gated stages: terraform scale -> wait for nodes Ready -> helm deploy. Add an explicit wait-for-nodes job that polls `kubectl get nodes --selector=redwood/gpu=true -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.conditions[?(@.type==\"Ready\")].status}'`.
maria: can we also use a lightweight lock service? deploy-bot supports creating locks via comments but that's manual. We have `deploy-lock` internal action — use it in workflows to acquire a named lock for `gpu-pool-${{ github.ref }}`.
sam: created a quick PR with the concurrency change + deploy-lock usage. But still worried about cache/corruption: our gha cache restore sometimes pulls an old `.terraform` state snapshot causing plan diffs. There's also a race if state backend updates are slightly delayed.
anya: we should ensure `terraform init` uses remote state backend strictly and avoid relying on cached providers/state between jobs. Add `-reconfigure` flag and remove TF cache from GHA cache keys.
kevin: note on costs: when nodepool gets scaled by accident we burn expensive GPU capacity. This happened yesterday for ~15 minutes and cost spike hit the billing alerts. We need guardrails: a max-scale limit and an approval step for >N GPUs.
maria: agree — add a policy check in CI: if planned change > 4 gpus then require `approvers: [infra-oncall]`. Implement with `github/codeql` style check or a simple action that parses terraform plan output.
anya: for immediate mitigation I'm going to pause automatic apply on `main` merges for gpu nodepool paths and switch to manual apply for the next 24h while we roll the fix.
sam: ack. I'll post the PR link in #eng-infra and update the workflow.
deploy-bot: deployment lock acquired: gpu-pool-main by sam at 2026-03-08T12:41:00Z :lock: (expires in 60m)
kevin: after fixes, let's run a dry-run against the staging nodepool to validate lock + wait logic.
maria: one more follow-up: add retries with exponential backoff on provider API failures (RequestLimitExceeded). terraform has provider `max_retries` for some providers; check and enable where available.
anya: thanks — will do a checklist: 1) tighten GHA concurrency + use deploy-lock, 2) split terraform scale & helm deploy, 3) remove TF state from caches and add `-reconfigure`, 4) add plan-based approval gate for >4 GPUs, 5) enable provider retries. I'll ping when PRs merged. :white_check_mark:
kevin: thanks team.
anya: filing a short incident note for cost spike + root cause so finance knows.
